Seven floors devoted to Pittsburgh-born Andy Warhol — the largest single-artist museum in North America, from the soup cans to the floating Silver Clouds room.
A museum of room-sized, permanent installation art you walk through — Yayoi Kusama's mirrored infinity room among them — in a former mattress warehouse on the North Side.

Pennsylvania's largest history museum and a Smithsonian affiliate — six floors on Pittsburgh's steel, glass and sports story, the Heinz 57 kitchen, a real Mister Rogers set, and the Western PA Sports Museum.

A hop-forward Sharpsburg brewery beer nerds cross town for — hazy IPAs done with real precision in a relaxed taproom.
A well-loved Millvale brewery with a big outdoor deck and rotating small-batch beers — the kind of neighbourhood taproom Pittsburgh does well.
Strip District production brewery and taproom with chef-driven pub food, best known for its Squish-series hazy IPAs and crisp house lagers.

Squirrel Hill tavern pouring only fresh, independent Western PA beer alongside locally sourced comfort food
Dual-concept cocktail bar and Alpine beer hall in the historic Werner Building on the East Liberty corner
The 'Squirrel Cage,' a 1935 art-deco dive on Forbes with cheap drinks, big burgers and cult status
A pioneer of Pittsburgh craft beer with a big Larimer taproom — ~14 taps, pinball, food trucks and easy parking — a proper neighbourhood beer hall.
Squirrel Hill tiki bar and repeat City Paper Best Craft Cocktails winner, pouring elaborate drinks from 500-plus rum bottlings with tropical juices pressed in house.
Bloomfield corner store and bar pouring an all-organic, biodynamic natural-wine list, plus bottled old fashioneds to drink in or take away.
Bloomfield brewery, bottle shop and community hangout on Main Street pouring hop-forward IPAs and mixed-culture farmhouse ales, with a food truck out front nightly.
Baking since 1926 — some 10,000 loaves a day — famous for a hand-rolled Italian 'twist' bread and fast-selling pepperoni rolls.
A seasonal cart on the same North Side spot since 1934 — hand-shaved ice balls in syrup, plus peanuts and popcorn — with an honorary 'Gus & YiaYia Way' named for it.
A hole-in-the-wall Strip bakery-café turning out biscotti and rustic breads from an old brick oven, with a hidden courtyard café out back.
A 1923 soda fountain restored to its original marble-and-mahogany glory in the Strip — sundaes, egg creams and banana splits in a genuine time capsule.
Home of the Burnt Almond Torte — once called 'the greatest cake in America' — a yellow cake with custard and caramelised almonds that Pittsburghers ship across the country.
A French patisserie from Master Pastry Chef David Piquard — jewel-like macarons and rum canelés — the sweet anchor of Squirrel Hill's Forbes Avenue.
A from-scratch French bakery (2010) — all-butter croissants and baguettes, plus quiches and tarts — with several locations across the city.
An Oakland institution since 1983 — hand-rolled waffle cones made on-site with an M&M plugged in the tip so nothing drips out.
A beloved small-batch scoop shop (with a cult 'honey lavender') that grew from a farmers'-market stand into several East End parlours.
Family French bakery in Regent Square turning out blistered, flaky croissants, baguettes and sweet pastries baked fresh daily.
A seasonal walk-up soft-serve stand by the river that opens every spring to long, happy lines — a South Side rite of warm weather since 1951.
A regional chocolatier since 1960 with a 1,500-pound edible chocolate castle and an old-fashioned parlour famous for sundaes capped in hardened poured chocolate.
